A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the free energies of binding of the two ligands are similar and hence the observed higher specificity of angiogin towards cytosines over uracils in the first base position is not a result of thermodynamic preference.

The main takeaway from our work is that

the binding free energy difference of 2.7 kcal/mol between the CMP and UMC ligands of bovine angiogenic is primarily due to the difference in the electrostatic contribution to the binding free energy of the two ligands.

the higher specificity of angioginin towards cytosine is a consequence of the higher free energy cost associated with the formation of the uracil-angiogenin hydrogen bond in comparison with the formation of a hydrogen bond between the protein and the cytosine.
the higher specificity of angiogenic activity of angiogenin can be attributed to the higher stability of the complex of angiogenin with CMP as compared to that of UMP.
